title: Evaluate eligibility rules as a tree

task.text: Marketing writes rules like `(and pro (not trial))`. Make each grammar rule a class that evaluates itself.
`Rule` is given: `boolean eval(Map<String, Boolean> flags)`. Fill in `Rules.java`.

items: `Flag(String name)` returns its flag, or throws `IllegalStateException` if the flag is unbound.
`Not(Rule)`, `And(Rule, Rule)` and `Or(Rule, Rule)` combine their children. `And` and `Or` must short-circuit.
`Rules.parse(String)` builds the tree from the text: a flag name, `(not r)`, `(and r r)` or `(or r r)`, with any amount of whitespace.
One parsed tree must evaluate against many contexts.

task.text: Do not change `Rule` or the constructors above.

checks.title: A flag reads the context, unbound flags fail
Not, And and Or follow their truth tables
And and Or skip the branch they do not need
One tree evaluates against many contexts
Parsed sentences give the right answers
Nodes evaluate without switching on types
Parsing builds the tree and stops there

hints.text: Each grammar rule is a class. A terminal answers directly from the context; a nonterminal asks its children and combines the answers. No central `switch` should decide how to evaluate.
Write `eval` in each record: `Flag` reads the map, `Not`, `And`, `Or` call `eval` on their children. For `parse`, read tokens recursively: `(` starts an operator, then its operands, then `)`.
